commit_message:
lavc/vvc: Add max parameter to kth_order_egk_decode

Prior to this patch, kth_order_egk_decode could read arbitrarily
large values which then overflowed and caused various issues.
Patch fixes this by making kth_order_egk_decode falliable,
requiring the caller to specify an upper bound and returning an
error if the read value would exceed that bound.

This patch resolves the same issue as
eb52251c0ab025b6b40b28994bc9dc616813b190, but I think this is the proper
fix as it also addresses issues with syntax elements besides
ff_vvc_num_signalled_palette_entries.

Signed-off-by: Frank Plowman <post@frankplowman.com>

findings.title: Signed integer overflow: coeff*scale multiplied before validating coeff
findings.message: In palette_subblock_data() (libavcodec/vvc/ctu.c), when decoding an escape-coded palette sample, ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() is called and can return a negative AVERROR value (e.g. AVERROR_INVALIDDATA) on malformed/corrupt bitstreams. The refactor in commit 7c5319e692 changed the escape-value API to be failable but reordered the code so that the returned 'coeff' is multiplied by 'scale' (coeff * scale) inside av_clip_intp2(RSHIFT(coeff * scale, 6), ...) BEFORE the 'if (coeff < 0) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;' check is performed. Since coeff can hold a large-magnitude negative error code, multiplying it by scale causes signed integer overflow, which is undefined behavior in C and was caught by OSS-Fuzz's UBSan (signed integer overflow: -1094995529 * 6528 cannot be represented in type 'int').
findings.suggestion: Validate the return value of ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() for an error/negative value before using it in any arithmetic (multiplication, shifting, clipping). Move the 'if (coeff < 0) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;' check immediately after the call and before computing 'pixel'.

ground_truth.root_cause: When ff_vvc_palette_escape_val() was made failable (returning negative AVERROR codes) as part of a broader refactor to bound Exp-Golomb decoding, the caller in palette_subblock_data() was updated to check the new error condition, but the validation check ('if (coeff < 0) return AVERROR_INVALIDDATA;') was placed after the arithmetic expression that uses 'coeff' in a multiplication, rather than before it. This ordering mistake allowed the invalid/error sentinel value to participate in signed multiplication, causing overflow.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: Signed integer overflow: coeff*scale multiplied before validating coeff
